patterns.title: No function keyword
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC does not use the `function` keyword. Just write the name followed by (). This is the same as CoD4 GSC.

patterns.title: No var/let/const declarations
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC has no variable declaration keywords. All variables are dynamically typed — just assign them.

patterns.title: No ternary operator
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC does not support the ternary operator ?:. Use if/else.

patterns.title: No arrow functions
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC does not support arrow functions (=>). Use named functions or inline for loops.

patterns.title: No template literals
patterns.right: msg = "Hello " + self.name + ", you have " + self.score + " points";
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC does not support template literals (backticks). Use + for string concatenation.

patterns.title: No .push() — use indexed append
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC arrays have no .push() method. Append by assigning to the index equal to .size.

patterns.title: No .length — use .size
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC uses .size (not .length) to get the number of elements in an array or string.

patterns.title: Iterating arrays — use indexed for loop
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC does not support for...of iteration. Always use an indexed for loop with .size.

patterns.title: No array destructuring
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC does not support destructuring assignment. Access array elements by index individually.

patterns.title: No object literals — use spawnstruct()
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC does not support object literal syntax {key: value}. Create a struct with spawnstruct() then assign properties.

patterns.title: No new keyword — use spawnstruct()
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC does not have a `new` keyword. Use spawnstruct() to create plain data objects.

patterns.title: Check property exists before accessing
patterns.explanation: Accessing an undefined property crashes IW4. Always guard with isDefined() before accessing nested properties.

patterns.title: Deleting a property
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC has no delete operator. Set the property to undefined to undefine it.

patterns.title: No null literal — use isDefined()
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC does not have a 'null' keyword. Use isDefined() or !isDefined() to check if a variable has a value.

patterns.title: No strict equality — use == and !=
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC does not support === or !==. Use == and != instead. All comparisons in IW4 are non-strict.

patterns.title: Converting types — use int() and float()
patterns.explanation: Use IW4's built-in int() and float() functions for type conversion, not JavaScript's parseInt/parseFloat.

patterns.title: Math functions — use built-ins not Math.*
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC has no Math object. Use int() for floor, abs() for absolute value, randomfloat()/randomint() for random numbers.

patterns.title: Infinite loop pattern
patterns.explanation: Both work in IW4, but for(;;) is the conventional infinite loop idiom in GSC. Always include a wait to avoid server freezing.

patterns.title: No forEach or .map()/.filter()
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC has no functional array methods. Build result arrays manually with indexed for loops.

patterns.title: Always wait inside infinite loops
patterns.explanation: Any infinite loop MUST have at least one wait call per iteration. Without it, the server will freeze and disconnect all players.

patterns.title: waittill must be called on an entity
patterns.explanation: waittill must always be prefixed with an entity (level, self, game, or a player entity). Bare waittill() is invalid.

patterns.title: waittill unpacks into local variables
patterns.right:
self waittill("damage", amount, attacker, sMeansOfDeath);
// now attacker is available
patterns.explanation: waittill() passes event data as additional local variables. List them after the event name string to capture them.

patterns.title: endon must be called on an entity
patterns.explanation: endon must always be prefixed with an entity. It terminates the current thread when the specified event fires on that entity.

patterns.title: Use thread for async operations
patterns.wrong:
// This blocks the calling function
watchAllPlayers();
patterns.right:
// This runs concurrently
level thread watchAllPlayers();
patterns.explanation: Use 'thread' to spawn non-blocking concurrent execution. Without it, the calling function is blocked until the callee returns.

patterns.title: notify broadcasts an event on an entity
patterns.explanation: notify must always be called on an entity. The entity is the channel — waittill listeners on the same entity will wake up.

patterns.title: No 'this' — use 'self'
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC has no 'this' keyword. When a function is called on an entity (e.g., player damagePlayer()), use 'self' to refer to that entity.

patterns.title: Check if player is alive with isAlive()
patterns.explanation: Use isAlive() instead of checking health > 0. Players can have health > 0 while still in the dying state.

patterns.title: String concatenation with +
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC supports the + operator for string concatenation. There is no .concat() method.

patterns.title: Printing to players — use iprintln not println
patterns.explanation: println() only prints to the server console. Use iprintln() for screen messages or iprintlnbold() for bold centered messages to players.

patterns.title: Getting all players — use getplayers()
patterns.right:
players = getplayers();
for (i = 0; i < players.size; i++) {}
patterns.explanation: Always use getplayers() to get the current list of connected players. level.players may not be defined or up to date.
